To: Renters Board / Notices
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT FOR REVIEW — Stop using Brightline Pro 6% batch LX2291

DRAFT ONLY — not for posting until I’ve checked it.

Everyone, please check your developer before your next colour. Kelvin Trade has confirmed a filling error affecting Brightline Pro 6% (20 vol) Cream Developer 1L, batch LX2291. Bottles labelled 6% may actually contain 12% (40 vol). This is a safety issue, not just an inconvenience.

WHICH BOTTLES TO CHECK

The affected batch is LX2291, supplied between 19 October and 5 November 2026.

Check the BASE OF EACH BOTTLE. The batch isn’t on the box, so checking the carton isn’t enough. Please check the open bottles in your trolley as well as unopened stock in the back. Don’t assume an open bottle is fine because you’ve used it already.

Kelvin Trade says other batches and other strengths are not affected. If you can’t read the code, put the bottle aside and get it checked with the supplier before using it.

IF YOU FIND LX2291

Stop using it immediately. Don’t try to dilute it, adjust your mixing ratio or use it up on a different service. Keep it separate from usable stock, clearly marked “DO NOT USE — LX2291”, so nobody picks it up by mistake.

The Kelvin Trade rep is in on Tuesday 10 November. Affected bottles can go back to him or to the Hillington depot for a full credit.

IMPORTANT: if you’ve had a problem with a bottle, keep that bottle back as evidence rather than handing it over with the returns. Don’t bin it or empty it out. Keep the label and batch code intact, store it safely and retain your purchase details and the supplier email. Photograph the bottle, label and base.

WHAT WE’VE SEEN / WHAT IT CAN DO

I had a client develop burning and visible scalp redness during a bleach retouch on Saturday using a new bottle from LX2291. The lift was much faster than usual and I stopped the service and rinsed immediately.

Another renter has confirmed the same batch after unusually fast lift and very hot foils on Thursday. Don’t assume excess heat is just the heater.

Developer stronger than intended can make a bleach mix lift faster and behave more aggressively than expected, increasing the risk of scalp burns, irritation, over-processing and hair breakage. Uneven results can happen too. Fast lift or hot foils don’t prove a bottle is affected: check the code, and don’t wait for a reaction before taking this batch out of use.

IF SOMEONE REACTS IN THE CHAIR

Stop the service immediately. Take burning, unexpected heat or pain seriously.

For a suspected chemical burn:
• Call 999 for medical help immediately. Don’t wait for blistering or severe pain.
• Protect yourself with gloves. Carefully remove contaminated clothing if possible.
• Rinse the affected area with plenty of cool or lukewarm running water for about ONE HOUR. Follow the call handler’s instructions.
• Don’t shampoo or apply creams, oils, aloe, neutralisers or other chemicals.
• Chemical burns need hospital assessment. Breathing difficulty, throat swelling or collapse also mean 999 immediately.

This follows the NHS chemical-burn guidance linked in our “Patch tests and skin tests” page. A patch test is not a way to clear a suspect bottle for use.

Once urgent care is underway, record what happened in the incident book: product, batch, mix, timings, symptoms and action taken. Keep detailed client records and any photographs private, not on this board.

Please check every bottle today and let the other renters know, especially anyone buying from the same rep.

Kirsty
